message.content:
At a pressure of **10 kPa** (≈ 0.098 atm), the melting/freezing point of pure water is slightly below the normal 0 °C.  
Using the water phase diagram, the solid–liquid equilibrium line at this pressure corresponds to a temperature of roughly **272.5 K**, which is about **–0.65 °C**.

So, the freezing point of water at 10 kPa is approximately **–0.6 °C**.
